original.target_description: Unresolved target: identity integration/consolidation in relation to open-mindedness. Figure 3 tests Openness/complexity against Identity Acceptance, whereas Figure 2 tests Capacity for Status against Identity Integration; neither establishes the supplied integration–open-mindedness pairing.

replication.target_description: Unassigned replication side; not examined in this source-grouped completion.

notes: PDF page 9 (printed p. 1003) rendered and visually checked. Table 4 predicts identity integration and acceptance from Environmental Mastery (EM), Personal Growth (PG), and EM x PG; it does not give a trait-to-integration test for either supplied trait description. Table 4 standardized integration coefficients are .22 (EM), .27 (PG), and -.04 (interaction), with N = 96; stars on .22 and .27 denote p < .05. These are candidate neighboring tests only, not assigned target values. Figure 2 instead links Capacity for Status at age 21 to Identity Integration at age 43 (.44, p < .05; N = 94). Figure 3 links Openness/complexity at age 21 to Identity Acceptance at age 43 (-.50, p < .05; N = 94). The two distinct identity dimensions are defined in Methods, pp. 999–1000. No coefficient conversion, N arithmetic, or inference from df was performed. All candidate Ns count women/participants in the named analyses; target-specific exclusions cannot be established. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. The related Openness index is explicitly documented as a composite of Creative Temperament, Tolerance of Ambiguity, and reversed Repression (p. 1000). Figure 3 is a possible nearby openness test but its mediator is identity acceptance, not integration; it cannot be silently substituted. Its -.50 standardized path with p < .05 and model N = 94 remain candidates only. Table 4 has N = 96 and EM/PG predictors, so that N is not established for the requested trait relationship.
